quote.quote: A Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) meeting was held on April 7, 2010, during review of the original NDA.

A pulmonary allergy drug advisory committee (PADAC) meeting was convened during the first review cycle on April 7, 2010, to discuss the efficacy and safety data provided to support the approval of roflumilast for the treatment of COPD in the United States.

recommendation.text: The committee voted favorably on efficacy (9 yes, 6 no) and on the safety profile (9 yes, 6 no), but voted against approvability (5 yes, 10 no). The product was nonetheless approved in a later review cycle with a narrowed indication, a Medication Guide-only REMS, and an add-on postmarketing commitment.

quote.quote: The committee voted favorably regarding whether there was substantial evidence of efficacy (9 yes, 6 no), and the safety profile of roflumilast (9 yes, 6 no). Regarding the approvability question, which is essentially the sum of demonstration of efficacy and safety, the results were against approval (5 yes, 10 no).

linkages.concern: Committee members indicated they would be more favorable on efficacy and approvability if the indication were the more restrictive, exacerbation-specific indication rather than the broad original COPD indication.
linkages.change: The indication was narrowed from the broad COPD claim to reducing the risk of COPD exacerbations in patients with severe COPD associated with chronic bronchitis and a history of exacerbations.

summary: A Pulmonary-Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee (PADAC) met on April 7, 2010 during the first review cycle and, voting against the broad original COPD indication, favored efficacy (9-6) and safety (9-6) but voted against approvability (5-10). Members said they would be more favorable with a more restrictive indication and that a risk mitigation strategy should be developed. Roflumilast (Daliresp) was ultimately approved in a later cycle with the indication narrowed to severe COPD with chronic bronchitis and a history of exacerbations and with a Medication Guide-only REMS; the Office Director's memo states these decisions were in keeping with the advice of a majority of the advisory committee members.
